newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower on interbank selling.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower on interbank selling.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended on its lows on Monday, due in part to interbank selling, but was expected to find support at current levels, dealers said.
The dollar closed at US$0.6912/17, down from 0.6940/47 near the start of the session, having traded a 0.6915-50 range.
The Trade-Weighted Index was at 67.32 from 67.48.

"It's our view that it will remain reasonably well bid here," said one Auckland dealer. "If we look at the TWI where it is, the MCI index, all those things put together should see the Kiwi bought from here."
Part of the Kiwi's softness could be attributed to weakness in U.S. dollar/yen.
"Maybe the interbank market got caught a little long. Having said that, we still believe the Kiwi will remain bid at the 0.6915 area," he said.
